trajectory_summary: This call moves steadily upward with no real friction: the customer is cooperative from the start and becomes increasingly engaged as he supplies unusually detailed data (tax-purpose annual bill figure, full 12-month kWh readout). The rep runs the verify sequence in order, captures the bill, and books a specific day and time with a live-request confirmation. The main gaps are underuse of the rich data the customer volunteered and a thin button-up, not any customer resistance.

observed_outcome.quote: Alright. Monday would be the twenty seventh... Monday, I'll put 3PM. It should work.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Monday the 27th) and time (3PM) were agreed for the closer's follow-up call, with the rep confirming a live-request double-check — this meets the bar for booked with a phone channel.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: bill anchor captured but never flipped
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Well, good point. In the wintertime, it has gone to $500 a month... somewhere between 3,500 and $4,000.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer gave one of the strongest bill anchors possible (specific annual figure, seasonal swing) and the rep filed it without reflecting it back as the reason to act — a five-second flip was available and never used through booking or button-up.

key_moments.quote: Well, I don't know. I might have just popped up an ad sometime and replied to it, but, I have looked from time to time about solar for the house.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer gives a vague, low-conviction reason ('I don't know... might have popped up an ad'). Reactive read: rep should have probed further to surface a real motivator (bill pain, curiosity, etc.) before moving on. Strategic read: the rep may have judged there was no usable thread here and prioritized moving to verified data (address, roof) where he could build real momentum — which he then did successfully via the bill numbers. Given the rep never returns to interest at all, even loosely, during booking or button-up, the reactive read is better supported: this was a genuine miss, not a deliberate deferral, because there's no later moment where 'interest in solar' resurfaces as leverage.

key_moments.quote: Well, actually, the house is in a partnership with my sister and me, but I'm the general partner, the one who runs everything.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer discloses a co-owner (sister) on the title. Rep's response ('You're kind of, the boss there') accepts the customer's framing that he alone runs things and does not ask whether the sister should be included on the appointment.

key_moments.quote: Well, good point. In the wintertime, it has gone to $500 a month. I just got one to this past month with a little over 200... somewhere between 3,500 and $4,000.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer hands over a rich, specific bill figure — a strong anchor for pain (annual cost, seasonal swing up to $500/month). Rep's response ('Oh, really? Okay. That makes sense... Thank you for kinda clarifying') acknowledges the number but files it rather than flipping it into an emotional or comparative frame ('so solar could level that $500 winter spike out'). Adjudicating strategic vs reactive: there is no later moment in the call where the rep references this figure again — not at booking, not at button-up — so this is a genuine missed flip rather than a deliberate deferral to the closer, since the rep had every opportunity in the button-up to tie the appointment to this pain point and did not.

key_moments.quote: On it says kilowatt hours and then it has the month. So you want the kilowatt hours per month?
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer not only has his bill archived but proactively organizes and reads off a full 12-month usage history unprompted. This is a highly cooperative, detail-oriented customer profile — a strong signal of genuine intent, not just idle curiosity.
